scope: Pattern B investigation from client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' - enumerate actor classes whose vftable[9] handles the Actor cluster opcodes that FUN_004DC690's generic fallthrough case (BCS-Y-0527) dispatches via `actor->vftable[+0x24]`. Started as 'document the per-actor-class taxonomy' but the investigation produced a CORRECTIVE finding: the vftable[9] dispatch is effectively a no-op for the known actor class hierarchies. Pattern B's 'polymorphic per-actor-class' framing was wrong and is corrected here.

key_findings.title: Control:: actor classes share a NO-OP vftable[9] stub
key_findings.detail: All 4 cataloged Control:: actor classes (CharaBase, PlayerBase, NpcBase, MyPlayer) share vftable[9] = FUN_005c5c80, a 3-byte `return 0` function with no callers per Ghidra's reference analysis. The slot exists in the vtable layout but is not used by any direct caller and no subclass overrides it.
key_findings.implication: If FUN_004d9910 returns a Control:: actor class, FUN_004DC690's generic fallthrough case (BCS-Y-0527) would invoke a no-op for all 24 Actor cluster opcodes - which contradicts the observation that these packets clearly have effects (MoveActor at 2176 pcap hits, etc.).

key_findings.title: Engine-side CharaActor::vftable[9] is a Scene-graph helper, NOT a packet handler
key_findings.detail: Application::Scene::Actor::Chara::CharaActor (the engine-side actor distinct from Lua-side Control::CharaBase) has vftable[9] = FUN_00621430 which is SQEX::CDev::Engine::Fw::SceneObject::Actor::AddReferenceResourceListener - a Scene-graph resource lifecycle method, not anything to do with s2c packet processing.
key_findings.implication: Neither the Lua-side nor the engine-side actor hierarchy I've inspected has a real packet handler at vftable[9]. The 'actor->vftable[+0x24]' dispatch in BCS-Y-0527 is effectively a no-op for currently known actor types.

key_findings.title: Pattern B's 'polymorphic per actor class' claim is wrong
key_findings.detail: An earlier finding stated that the 24 Actor cluster opcodes (0x0F + 0xCC..0xE5) dispatch via `actor->vftable[9](packet)` and the per-actor-class slot 9 implementation handles them. The actor-vftable9-investigation pass demonstrates this is not the case for any cataloged actor class - all known actor slot 9 implementations are either no-op stubs (Control::*) or unrelated Scene-graph methods (CharaActor). The dispatcher case fires but the dispatched function does nothing related to the packet.
key_findings.implication: Either (a) the actual packet handling lives elsewhere (a different dispatcher, side-effects of FUN_004d9910 lookup, or engine-internal animation/position predictors that subscribe to actor state changes via a different mechanism); or (b) the slot 9 dispatch is genuinely vestigial in 1.23b and the engine processes these packets without acting on them (server-authoritative state is recorded but visual updates use a parallel system); or (c) there's a derived actor class not in the catalog that DOES override slot 9 with a real implementation. Resolving this requires either live capture or finding the actor class that FUN_004d9910 actually returns via inspecting how the actor map at zone+0x17804 is populated.

pattern_b_correction.before: Pattern B: Generic actor `vftable[9]` (the actor-cluster-dispatch-model pass). For 24 opcodes (`0x0F + 0xCC + 0xCD + 0xCE + 0xCF + 0xD0 + 0xD3..0xE5`) the dispatcher does `actor = FUN_004d9910(packet_actor_id); actor->vftable[9](packet)`. The actor's slot 9 is the per-actor-class polymorphic handler that interprets opcode and payload based on actor type.
pattern_b_correction.after: Pattern B: Generic actor `vftable[9]` (actor_cluster_dispatch_model.json+actor_vftable9_investigation.json). For 24 opcodes (`0x0F + 0xCC + 0xCD + 0xCE + 0xCF + 0xD0 + 0xD3..0xE5`) the dispatcher does `actor = FUN_004d9910(packet_actor_id); actor->vftable[9](packet)`. **The actor-vftable9-investigation pass finding**: this dispatch appears to be a no-op for known actor class hierarchies - Control:: classes share a 3-byte `return 0` stub at slot 9 (BCS-Y-0528 FUN_005C5C80, 0 callers); engine-side CharaActor's slot 9 is a Scene-graph resource lifecycle method (BCS-Y-0529 FUN_00621430, AddReferenceResourceListener) unrelated to packet processing. The actual processing of MoveActor / SetActorPosition / etc. likely happens elsewhere (alternative dispatcher, side-effects of FUN_004d9910's map lookup, or engine-internal position/animation predictors) - identifying it requires live capture (deferred) or following how the actor map at zone+0x17804 is populated to determine the actual class hierarchy FUN_004d9910 returns. The 'polymorphic per-actor-class' framing from the actor-cluster-dispatch-model pass was inferred from the call shape but does not match observed slot 9 implementations - either some actor subclass not in the catalog overrides slot 9 with a real handler, or the dispatch is genuinely vestigial in 1.23b.
